_meta.description: Retrieval eval set for ContextIQ's hybrid (FAISS + BM25 EnsembleRetriever) search.
READ_ME_BEFORE_CITING: Your dev environment had almost no indexed data when this was built (6 chunks total, only txt/csv/md, no pdf/docx). To get all 5 file types covered, a small SYNTHETIC 10-document corpus (eval/fixtures/*, ~17 chunks) was written and ingested into a dedicated eval user (user_id=9001, see eval/config.py) via the app's own unmodified ingestion pipeline (see eval/build_eval_corpus.py).

Because the corpus is synthetic and authored by the assistant, ground truth relevant_chunk_ids below were assigned with high confidence by directly reading the actual indexed chunk text (see eval/build_eval_corpus.py output) rather than guessed blind -- each entry is marked verified=true on that basis. Still spot-check a sample yourself before citing numbers publicly; 'verified' here means 'traced to real chunk content', not 'independently reviewed by you'.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT for citing results: this corpus is tiny (17 chunks, 10 documents). Precision/Recall/MRR/MAP numbers on a 17-chunk corpus are illustrative of hybrid-vs-single-retriever BEHAVIOR (e.g. exact-number/rare-term lookups favoring BM25/hybrid over pure vector search), not a claim about performance at production scale. If you cite these publicly, say so -- e.g. 'on a controlled 17-chunk, 5-file-type benchmark' rather than implying a large-scale production benchmark.

chunk_id format: '<file_name>::<index>', where index is the chunk's 0-based position within that file's chunk list, in the order build_eval_corpus.py ingested it. Not a field the app stores itself -- reconstructed identically in run_eval.py from the persisted chunks.pkl order.
